Updates

v41 · Gift codes Latest

  • Gift codes. Got a code from the game’s owner? Type it under Cards on the main menu to get the card it holds. Each code works once for each player.
  • The owner can also hand out cards live to people who are playing right now.

v40 · Teammate markers fixed

  • Teammates' names are now flat markers on your screen: always the same size, never cut off by walls or ceilings, a little dimmer when a wall is between you, and pinned to the edge of the screen with an arrow when they are off to the side or behind you. They also say when a teammate is down or hiding.
  • Teammates move smoothly. They used to lurch and stutter when their updates arrived unevenly, and slide through walls after a respawn. Now they glide between the places we last heard they were, and jump straight to a new spot after a respawn or a door.
  • Pings and other markers more than 60 m away no longer flip to the wrong side of the screen.

v39 · A big round of fixes

  • The map shows the doors between rooms (red while shut, green once open), the name of every room you have been in, and a star on the room the next entity is in.
  • The Journal now has Level 3 (it said 0 of 31 when there are 40), and every level lists its entities in the order you face them. The Scare Museum has Level 3 and the Flesh Stealer too.
  • On screens that are not very wide, your health no longer sits on top of the tool bar, and in the tutorial messages no longer cover the tutorial card.
  • Dash shows as locked until Snackbot teaches it to you.
  • The tutorial's Stillman fight is practice now. It used to put him in your Journal out of order.
  • Every run starts at Level 0. The level picker still shows every level and your best times, but starting always drops you into Level 0. Escape each level to go down to the next one. Co-op games start at Level 0 too, and you can still join a friend wherever they are.
  • Level 1's gate to the Poolrooms stays shut until you beat the Valet, like every other door. It used to be open from the start.
  • A lot of old text was brought up to date.

v38 · Everyone starts again

  • All progress was reset for every player: levels, moves, cards, tokens, the journal and records. Everyone starts at Level 0 with no sprint, dash or jump. Settings, controls and names were kept. Save codes from before this update no longer load.
  • Fix: the Static Hound's radios, and anything else a fight puts down, could land on the far side of a wall, in an area that was still locked. They now always go somewhere you can walk to.
  • Jump stays locked until Mr. Confetti teaches it to you, on every level.

v37 · One level at a time

  • Levels open in order. Level 0 is always open. Escape it to open Level 1, escape that to open Level 2, and so on. Once a level is open you can start there from the main menu any time.
  • If you have already escaped a level before, the levels after it are open for you.
  • You can still join a friend's game on any level. Hosting needs the level open.

v36 · Doors you can read

  • Every door has a proper sign on both sides with the name of the room behind it, and it sinks into the floor when it opens. The Concrete Garden gets rusted roller shutters.
  • A trail of light runs from you to each door the moment it opens.
  • Area titles. The first time you step into an area its name comes up across the screen.
  • New moves get a moment of their own: light, a ring going out from you, the name dropping in letter by letter. Then try it out for 3 card tokens.
  • Flawless. Beat an entity without taking a hit for 2 card tokens.
  • Checkpoints. If something gets you, you come to at the door of the area you were in, not back at the start of the level.
  • Touch screens get Jump, Ping and both ability-card buttons, and crouching while you run slides.

v35 · Rooms behind doors

  • Levels 1, 2 and 3 are rooms behind doors now, like Level 0. Each level is split into areas, each its own maze around its room, and a locked door leads on to the next area when you document the entity in this one.
  • Level 1 starts in the north-west corner of the Garage and runs through Crate Storage, the Ticket Booth, the Stairwell, the Car Park, the Flooded Bay and the Valet Lot, then through the gate into the Poolrooms.
  • Level 2 goes round the Party Room in a spiral, starting with the Balloon Man at the party table.
  • Level 3 starts at the mural courtyard and ends at the plaza and the garden.
  • Fixes. Entities could not catch you before your first dash, so the Static Hound walked into you and stood there. Things that roam no longer stand inside you while you are in another fight.

v33 · Every level in order

  • Rooms open in order on every level. On Levels 1, 2 and 3 each entity's room is fenced off with yellow and black tape until it is that entity's turn. The mazes, tubes and streets in between stay open to explore.
  • The Garage has rooms now: Crate Storage, the Stairwell, the Car Park and the Flooded Bay, and each of their entities is called from its own room.
  • The goal at the top points you to the next room, with how far away it is.

v32 · One room at a time

  • Entities come in order. Every level has a set order, and only the next one can be called. Your goal at the top always says who is next and how to find them.
  • Level 0 is rebuilt as eight themed rooms, each in its own maze: the Static Room, the Vending Alcove, the Party Room, the Door Corridor, the Pillar Hall, the Dark Office, the Long Hallway and the Front Desk. A door opens to the next area when you document the entity in this one.
  • Earn your moves. You start with no sprint, dash or jump. The Static Hound teaches you to sprint, Snackbot to dash and Mr. Confetti to jump. Later, the Valet teaches you to slide and the Lifeguard to swim. They are yours for good. If you had already beaten them, you have them already.
  • Jumping works on every level, and the mazes after the Party Room have low walls to jump. Nothing that walks can follow you over.
  • Seven entities give an ability card the first time you beat them: Wide Beam (the Lampmoth), Hold Breath (the Undertow), Float (the Balloon Man), Double Jump (Come-Play), Silent Steps (Tallgrass), High Jump (the Stilt) and Ground Pound (the Groundskeeper).

v31 · The daily shop

  • Today's cards. The card shop sells three set cards a day, each at its own price. Everyone gets the same three, and they change at midnight UTC. Each one can be bought once a day.
  • Random card. 25 card tokens for a random card, three rolls at a time. Escaping a level fills them up again. It works from the main menu too.
  • The Flesh Stealers. Three of them now walk the parking garage on Level 1. They come to light and noise. Flash each one to document them, or turn your light off and crouch to slip past.
  • Fixes. The roll button in the card shop always responds now, and tells you why when it can't roll.

v30 · Play together

  • Pings. Press B (or the middle mouse button) to mark the spot you're aiming at, an entity or an item, for everyone in your room. Every marker shows how far away it is in meters, and so do teammates in the corner of your screen and the arrows on fight hints.
  • Drop items. G drops a battery and H drops Fizz Water for a teammate to pick up.
  • Flash with care. Your flash now blinds teammates who are in front of you, for up to a few seconds depending on how close they are.
  • The Sun burns hotter on a crowd. Standing close together heats you up faster, and the shade cools a crowd more slowly.
  • Combine cards. Two copies of a stackable card combine into one at the next level with double the effect, for example 7% less damage becomes 14%. Every card says how far it stacks.
  • Three loadouts, each with its own cards and abilities.
  • Mystery roll. A random card in the card shop, three times on every level. Luck makes the rarer cards more likely.
  • Seven new cards: Spare Bulb (+1 flash charge), Thick Skin (+20 max health), Static Charm (a chance to switch an entity off for its first round), Big Binder (+2 card slots), Four-Leaf (+10% luck), Molasses (entities move slower) and Pogo Insoles (jump higher, Level 3 and up).
  • Twelve ability cards with their own keys (Z and X) and cooldowns: Sugar Rush, Pocket Medkit, Prank Call, Grab Bag, Dowsing Rod, Static Burst, Green Wall, Vanish, Decoy Radio, Red String, Pop-Up Shop and Teleport Pads.
  • Fixes. The battery slot no longer says R, which is the Flash key now.

v29 · Nicer cards, more garden

  • Cards look better. Corner ornaments, a light sheen on Rare and up, gold rays behind Legendary art, a slowly turning holographic edge on Godly cards, and Entity cards with a bigger, flickering portrait and a REC stamp.
  • Entity cards are better. Bigger upsides and a much smaller catch on every one.
  • Three more entities in the Concrete Garden: the Bloom, Rush Hour and the Creeper. The Groundskeeper now wakes once you have documented any five of the other eight.
  • Change cards from the map. Open the map [M] in a run and press Change cards.
  • A simpler main menu. Play together sits right beside Play. The Scare museum is inside the Journal, and Account, Settings and Records are together under Profile.

v28 · The Concrete Garden

  • Level 3: the Concrete Garden. A city that nature took back, with six new entities that are harder than anything before: the Stilt, the Rootmother, the Brutalist, Tallgrass, the Signal and the Groundskeeper.
  • Jumping. Locked until you beat the Stilt, then yours for good. Press Space. Level 3 has ditches, islands, planters and a broken parking deck to jump.
  • Cards. New odds: Common 75%, Rare 20%, Legendary 4%, Godly 1%, plus a 5% Entity card on top. Every card now opens with a reveal that gets louder the rarer it is.
  • Lucky Roll. Finish a level and spin for a Rare (65%), Legendary (25%) or Godly (10%) card.
  • Card shop and trading. Sell cards for blue card tokens and buy random cards with them. Trade cards with friends: hold E on a teammate, or use Trade cards in the pause menu.
  • Two tokens. Blue card tokens turn up on every level and stay with your account. Red vending tokens are Level 0 only and only work in its vending machine. Old tokens became card tokens.
  • Controls. Q dashes, Space jumps, R flashes. Every key can be changed in Settings.
  • Something rare. Every so often, while you're exploring, everything goes quiet. It can't hurt you.
  • Fixes. Each player gets their own Copycat in co-op. VS mode catches now match what the hunter sees and never go through walls. Coming back from a menu no longer spins the camera. Saves happen by themselves; save codes are only for moving to another device.

v27 · Cards you keep

  • Every entity you beat drops a card, kept in your inventory for good. Equip up to five.
  • Upgrades are gone; anything bought before came back as tokens.
  • All entities are summoned by their rituals again, and the Dread meter is gone.
  • Co-op: one shared fight when two players summon the same entity together, and the Static Hound no longer jitters.
  • The journal frees your mouse, and collected coins stay collected.

v26 and earlier

  • Accounts that need no sign-in, with save codes.
  • Knock-Knock's door lights up red when it knocks.
  • The Playground rebuilt smaller and scarier; every entity reworked into a real fight; VS Mode, the Scare Museum, level select and the tutorial.

Field Journal

Notes found ·

Tips

Entities come one at a time, in order, and only when you call them with their ritual. The notes give you clues. Beat the one in a room and the door to the next room opens. Come-Play on Level 2 and the Flesh Stealers on Level 1 come looking on their own. If something catches you, you lose health and wake at the door of the room you were in. Your Journal, moves and cards stay with you.
